title: Sunk Cost Awareness
hook: Already spending a year on something is not a reason to spend another one on it.
statement: Don't keep pouring effort into something just because you've already invested in it.
explainer: What you've spent is gone either way. Stopping doesn't waste it and continuing doesn't bring it back. The only thing that should decide is what happens from here.
sop: Set a checkpoint date for anything eating your time or money.
Score Future Benefit and Cost from 1 to 10, ignoring what's already spent.
If the number comes out negative, stop, no matter what went in.
Move that freed-up time and money to something positive.
Write down why you stopped so you don't quietly restart it.
equation_example: Future Benefit 3 minus Cost 7 = negative 4. Stop, no matter how much you already put in. Future Benefit 8 minus Cost 3 = 5. Positive, so keep going. Positive means the road ahead is worth it. Negative means let it go.
question: Name one thing you're still doing only because of what you've already put into it.
closing_statement: Only the road ahead should decide if you keep going.
caption:
Principle Nº 236: Sunk Cost Awareness

Already spending a year on something is not a reason to spend another one on it.

Don't keep pouring effort into something just because you've already invested in it.

Your turn: Name one thing you're still doing only because of what you've already put into it.
